classification.difficultyReason: Read the normalised cubic root relations, form the square sum and interpret its negativity as excluding three real intercepts; fractional coefficients add no new decision.

content.prompt:
Let $2x^3+4x^2+7x-5=0$ have roots $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$.

(a) Find the value of $\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2$.

(b) Hence, explain why the graph of $y=2x^3+4x^2+7x-5$ cannot have 3 $x$-intercepts.

answer.short: (a) $-3$. (b) If all three roots were real, the sum of their squares would be non-negative. Since the sum is $-3$, the roots cannot all be real, so the graph cannot have 3 $x$-intercepts.
answer.worked:
(a)
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha+\beta+\gamma&=-\frac42=-2\\\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma+\beta\gamma&=\frac72\\\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2&=(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^2-2(\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma+\beta\gamma)\\&=(-2)^2-2\left(\frac72\right)\\&=-3\end{aligned}$$
(b) A cubic has three roots, counting multiplicity. If all three were real, $\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2\geq0$. Part a gives $\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=-3$, so the roots cannot all be real. Hence the graph cannot have 3 $x$-intercepts.
